thread:
satoshi: Aduja v0.2 is on canary and I ran the multilingual smoke suite. Quick heads-up: seeing a tokenization/detok oddity in JP+AR mixed samples after int8 quant — BLEU drop ~3.1 on the mix-orient subset.

nora: Oof. Can you paste a minimal repro example? :eyes:

satoshi: Example input we used:
```
日本語（漢字《ふりがな》）とArabic (مرحبا)
```
Model output (int8):
```
日本語（漢字《 ふ り が な 》）とArabic )مرحبا(
```

nora: Two things there — the furigana got space-split and the Arabic parentheses appear mirrored/rewound. Sounds like tokenization + bidi/detok mismatch.

maya: Is this present on fp16 baseline or only after quant?

satoshi: Baseline fp16 -> clean: no extra spaces in furigana and parentheses orientation correct. Issue emerges after int8 quant + our serving runtime path. Repro command I ran: `./eval/run_locale_smoke.sh --model aduja-v0.2 --quant int8 --subset mix-orient`

kai: Tokenizer is deterministic, so if tokens differ it's either a different vocab/merge ops or a post-decode detok transform. Could quant change decoding tokenization? Unlikely but decode-time byte handling could.

satoshi: Agreed. My hunch is post-decode detok in the runtime — maybe we strip or normalize ZWJ/ZWNJ or run the Unicode bidi step incorrectly for mixed-direction strings after certain kernel outputs. Attached tiny hex log from canary decode: `... e3 81 8b 20 e3 81 95 ...` shows inserted 0x20 around ruby.

eval-bot: [automated] job 1749532100-A completed: subset=mix-orient, BLEU(fp16)=28.4, BLEU(int8)=25.3, chrF(fp16)=0.62, chrF(int8)=0.58, sample_mismatch=89/1000. See sample ids: 12, 47, 102...

zane: Can someone run the local tokenizer inspect on that snippet? `python -m token_inspect --text "漢字《ふりがな》" --model-tokenizer path/to/aduja-tokenizer` — want token ids + merges.

maya: I'm rerunning with kvcache disabled to rule out cache masking effects (since kvcache paths hit different kernels). Will report.

satoshi: FYI bracket mirroring only reproduces when Arabic portion is inside parentheses. So bidi algorithm result depends on exact codepoints around boundary. Tagging @nora @kai for runtime triage.

nora: I'll start a bisect across runtime commits between tags `runtime-2024-11-10`..`runtime-2024-11-20` — saw a detok libc bump in that window. Will post results.

kai: Also adding a small unit test: detok('...') for mixed-orient with explicit locale flags (LTR/RTR) to fail fast. If detok behavior changed, unit will catch it.

maya: Quick update: kvcache disable did NOT change the symptom. So less likely to be cache. I captured token boundaries in the int8 decode run: token ids around the ruby are different (off by one merge), which then leaves spaces after detok.

satoshi: Next steps: (1) add locale-aware detok regression test to runtime repo, (2) bisect runtime detok/path libc change, (3) test q5_0 and int4 to see if issue is quant-specific threshold. I'll open a tiny PR for the test now. :hammer_and_wrench: 

nora: Nice. If bisect points to libc, we can pin the old lib in canary until fix. Keep this thread updated; if anyone posts failing examples drop them here.

satoshi: Thanks all — I'll collect a short repro package with seeds + small subset and upload to the triage ticket. :thumbsup:
